transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-02-12
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: 62 minutes
Attendees: Aisha Patel, Marcus Chen, Priya Rao (Redwood); Evan Rodriguez, Linda Mo, Kunal Iyer, Sara Nguyen (NorthStar)

[00:00] Aisha Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um, we're running about an hour — appreciate you squeezing this in. Quick roll call?
[00:18] Evan Rodriguez: Evan here, hi all.
[00:21] Linda Mo: Linda.
[00:23] Kunal Iyer: Kunal on the line.
[00:25] Marcus Chen: Marcus here from Redwood infra.
[00:28] Priya Rao: Priya, partnerships.
[00:30] Aisha Patel: Great, cool. Quick agenda, co-sell playbook review, pipeline review — the six deals you flagged last week — and go over registration/MDF process and any technical asks.

[00:52] Evan Rodriguez: Sounds good. We want to focus on two enterprise deals where the customer is sensitive about data residency and one smaller SaaS that just needs low latency inference.
[01:08] Aisha Patel: Perfect. Marcus, want to take 2 minutes on the playbook changes?

[01:15] Marcus Chen: Yeah, sure. So we updated the playbook to clarify lead ownership when NorthStar does the intro — basically, initial SDR + NorthStar AE do joint intro, Redwood AE picks up after demo request. There's a simplified deal registration flow in the portal now — it's a short form and then a 72-hour review SLA. We also added two tech call templates: one for Dedicated (reserved capacity) and one for Private/VPC on-prem.
[01:47] Linda Mo: Nice, the 72-hour SLA helps. Previously it was unclear how long deal holds last.

[02:02] Aisha Patel: Yep. And we can special-case fast-tracked deals if it's an exec intro or co-sell motion with MDF attached.

[02:18] Evan Rodriguez: Question on MDF: is there a minimum commitment to tap budget? Also, are co-marketing activities co-funded or fully funded?

[02:35] Aisha Patel: For Q2 pilot MDF, we typically require a simple commitment — 6 months of reserved capacity or a 3-month mutual pipeline cadence. Co-marketing is typically matched 50/50 but we can make exceptions for strategic accounts.

[02:54] Kunal Iyer: Can you put that in the playbook as examples? Our sellers always want to show exact asks.

[03:07] Priya Rao: We'll add an MDF section with sample asks and templated language for partner reps to use.

[03:22] Sara Nguyen: Quick technical question — for the two deals requiring data residency in EU, does Redwood support private control plane in a customer VPC across AWS eu-west-1 and also on-prem? We need to be specific because their legal team will ask about key management.

[03:46] Marcus Chen: Yes, we support Private with customer-managed VPC in eu-west-1; on-prem is supported with our appliance packaging but depends on the air-gap constraints. KMS integration is available — we support customer KMS/HSM for key wrapping. Note that for on-prem you need a connectivity and support plan.

[04:08] Evan Rodriguez: How about SOC2 and audit logs?

[04:14] Marcus Chen: SOC2 Type II cert is available; audit logs can be exported to your SIEM. We'll share the security playbook link — it's in the partner portal reference.

[04:30] Aisha Patel: We'll attach SOC2 report as part of the security packet we share after this call.

[04:40] Evan Rodriguez: Great. Now pipeline — we pulled six deals, I'm going to run through them quickly.

[04:50] Evan Rodriguez: Deal A: FinanceTech EU large bank, potential TCV $1.1M, needs EU residency, timeline Q3. Deal B: RetailOps US — latency sensitive, needs sub-100ms, might prefer Dedicated in US-West. Deal C: HealthIS — needs HIPAA + on-prem; early-stage. Deal D: LogisticsCo — POC in progress, target go-live Q2, TCV $220k. Deal E: EduSoft startup — small POC, willing to be references. Deal F: AdPlatform — heavy embedding use, cost sensitivity.

[05:40] Aisha Patel: Thanks Evan. For Deal B, latency target sub-100ms — that suggests Dedicated in-region or edge-optimized routing; we should run a quick benchmark. Marcus can run estimated latency/cost numbers.

[05:56] Marcus Chen: Yep I can model continuous batching scenarios and expected p95 with Dedicated GPUs. I want to flag that for embedding-heavy workloads (Deal F) we recommend vector DB caching and batching — that reduces token cost.

[06:16] Linda Mo: On Deal C (HealthIS), they are very controls-heavy. Would Private on-prem be feasible? They may require no outbound traffic.

[06:28] Marcus Chen: On-prem possible but if it's air-gapped we need to confirm model updates policy — typically customers allow a sync window where we push model artifacts via secure transfer; fully disconnected is more complex and requires on-site ops support.

[06:45] Kunal Iyer: For deal registration, what's the hold period and how do we avoid duplicate submissions?

[06:53] Aisha Patel: Portal de-dupes by primary account domain and opportunity name; hold is 30 days by default, can extend on joint action. We'll add a note in playbook.

[07:08] Evan Rodriguez: Any objections from NorthStar sellers about the commission split? They asked about northstar fee vs reseller vs co-sell.

[07:18] Priya Rao: Our standard is 15% referral for pure intro, 10% for reseller with discounted ARR tiers; for co-sell we do split incentives based on seat and region. We should document examples.

[07:35] Linda Mo: Can we get an example calculator for margin and expected ACV for our reps?

[07:42] Aisha Patel: Yes, Marcus we'll add a simple sheet that shows net-to-partner and illustrative discounts.

[07:52] Marcus Chen: I'll add that. Also I'll add a short tech appendix comparing performance of our Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private for common workloads — e.g., chat generation 1k tokens typical latencies and cost per 1M tokens.

[08:10] Evan Rodriguez: Good. On the customer side, for Deal A (EU bank), what's the handoff to security? Do we need to do a security questionnaire?

[08:22] Aisha Patel: We often run a security questionnaire (SIG Lite) then SOC2 enclosed; for heavy regulated customers we do a deeper questionnaire and maybe on-site audit. We'll prep a security FAQ tailored for NorthStar to use with their customers.

[08:34] Sara Nguyen: About benchmarks — can Redwood do a small 2-hour latency/cost bench for Deal B? We can set up test keys and sample prompts.

[08:45] Marcus Chen: Yes, we can spin a quick dedicated bench for a POC — need sample prompt set and target SLAs. Put the bench ask in the joint doc and we'll prioritize.

[08:58] Evan Rodriguez: We'll add it. Next, co-marketing: Linda had suggested a joint webinar targeting RetailOps and FinTech — can Redwood support speaker and demo?

[09:09] Linda Mo: Yes, a 45-minute webinar with live demo would be ideal. We think we can drive 200 registrants.

[09:18] Aisha Patel: Redwood can provide demo dev time and a speaker. We'll add co-marketing tactical plan to portal — topics, assets, and promotional cadence. Linda, if you confirm the MDF ask we'll accelerate registration.

[09:34] Linda Mo: We'll review MDF internally and come back next week.

[09:40] Evan Rodriguez: Any competitive concerns? Customers sometimes ask about Anthropic and Lambda Labs integration costs.

[09:48] Marcus Chen: Competitors mentioned typically on model choice and pricing; our angle is predictable serving economics and unified runtime across hosted/dedicated/private — we should emphasize observability and rollout tools.

[10:05] Kunal Iyer: Also, call out model version pinning and rollback as a feature for product teams.

[10:12] Aisha Patel: Good call. We'll add messaging.

[10:20] Evan Rodriguez: Let's recap next steps.

[10:24] Aisha Patel: Recap: 1) I will share the playbook PDF and portal invite by Friday (2025-02-14). 2) Marcus will produce a short tech appendix and pricing/margin calculator by Monday (2025-02-17). 3) NorthStar will populate the joint pipeline sheet with six deals and TCV by Tuesday (2025-02-18). 4) Linda to confirm MDF availability by 2025-02-20. 5) Schedule exec intro for week of 2025-02-24.

[10:55] Evan Rodriguez: That works. Any other questions?

[11:00] Sara Nguyen: One last ask: can you include API rate limit and quota examples in the playbook for partner devs? They tend to hit limits during demos.

[11:08] Marcus Chen: Yes, add an FAQ section on quotas and throttling with example headers and expected 429 behavior.

[11:18] Aisha Patel: Awesome. Thanks everyone. We'll follow up via the joint pipeline doc and portal.

[11:24] Linda Mo: Thanks, talk soon.
[11:27] Kunal Iyer: Thanks all.

[11:30] Aisha Patel: Bye!

Notes on transcription: automated transcript had a few mis-hears (Dev Ops Bot insertion), some speaker overlaps, and occasional truncated words. Action items captured above.
